overview: T3 Code is a control surface that lets you manage AI coding agents like Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor from mobile, web, or desktop apps. It runs a local server on your machine and connects to agents you already have installed. Learners can study how a TypeScript project orchestrates multiple CLI tools and builds cross-platform clients.
how_to_start: Install and authenticate at least one AI agent (e.g., run `codex login` for Codex or `claude auth login` for Claude Code).
Install T3 Code via the command line: `curl -fsSL https://t3.codes/install.sh | sh` (or use the PowerShell command on Windows).
Run `t3` to start the server and open the local web app.
Optionally run `t3 service install` to keep it running in the background.

read_these.why: Step-by-step install and first-run guide with platform-specific details.
Answers common questions about providers, permissions, and troubleshooting.
Explains how to connect from a phone or another machine.
Starting point for understanding the codebase architecture if you want to build from source.
Rules for reporting bugs and opening PRs; the project notes it mostly does not accept contributions yet.

first_contributions: Fix a typo or clarify wording in the documentation under docs/.
Improve a small CLI help message or error output in the TypeScript source.
Add a missing keyboard shortcut to docs/user/keybindings.md.
Pick up the single open good-first-issue if it is still available.
watch_out: The project states it is very early and expects bugs.
Maintainers say they are mostly not accepting contributions; only small fixes may be considered.
High contributor count (945) but the project is only 273 days old, suggesting many drive-by contributions or a broad definition of contributor.
No dedicated documentation site yet; all docs live in the repository markdown files.
